title: Handling exceptions in CompletableFuture
context: How do you handle an exception in a CompletableFuture chain?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: An exception in any stage is passed along the chain and skips the later thenApply steps. Handle it with `exceptionally` for a fallback value, or `handle` to get the result or the exception and transform both. `whenComplete` runs for logging but doesn't change the result. Remember that join and get wrap the failure: join throws CompletionException and get throws ExecutionException, and the cause holds the original error.

points.title: Exceptions skip steps
points.why: A failed stage skips later thenApply calls until something handles the error.

points.title: Wrapped exceptions
points.why: join throws CompletionException and get throws ExecutionException, both wrapping the cause.
